source: Headers character-cost / request-id / x-trace-id: VERBATIM names from https://elevenlabs.io/docs/api-reference/introduction (code sample: rawResponse.headers.get('character-cost')); current-concurrent-requests / maximum-concurrent-requests: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/overview/models; x-region: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/eleven-api/guides/how-to/best-practices/latency-optimization. All accessed 2026-10-07. Body handling MEASURED with the real SDK 2.71.0 (probe-wire.out): convert() resolves to a web ReadableStream<Uint8Array>; withRawResponse() exposes the headers. Header VALUES and the Content-Type value are COMPOSED (not documented).

headers.content-type: audio/mpeg  <- GUESS, the docs do not state the value

sdkResult.rawResponse: { headers: Headers, status: 200, statusText, url, redirected, type }

expect.audio: SpeakResponse.audio = the whole body as Uint8Array
expect.mediaType: Derived from the requested output_format (as the openai provider does), not from the Content-Type header, whose value is undocumented.
expect.usage: Billing unit is characters. The billed count is the 'character-cost' response header (a decimal string). It can differ from input.length (per-model/per-voice multipliers, see GET /v1/models model_rates.character_cost_multiplier) - GUESS how exactly; whether whitespace/tags count is not documented. If the header is missing, coax has no measured value (input.length would be a guess, not the bill).
expect.notReachable: With plain await (no withRawResponse) the headers are lost - the provider must use withRawResponse() to report usage.
